term: almost-everywhere Euclidean and selected-reflexive validity under a supplied measure
definition: AlmostEverywhereModalValidity m w μ means that for μ-almost every θ, the frame of m θ is Euclidean and the selected w θ accesses itself. The conjunction is only required almost everywhere under THIS arbitrary supplied measure. It asserts no modal frame is actual, no probability normalization or uniform prior, and no positive mass of possible necessary beings. Euclidean here is the modal condition: R u v and R u z imply R v z; selected reflexivity is R (w θ) (w θ). Neither is a statement about spatial geometry.
